label: def:automated-discovery-certified-theory-state
title: Certified theory state
snippet: A certified theory state is a tuple $$ T=(S_{ T},P_{ T},L_{ T}, C_{ T},N_{ T}) $$ where $$ S_{ T},P_{ T},L_{ T}:Prop, C_{ T}:Prop, $$ and $$ N_{ T}: (S_{ T},P_{ T}, L_{ T},C_{ T}). $$ The five fields record source, pattern, ledger, classifier, and semantic naming certificate.

label: def:automated-discovery-automation-record
title: Automation record
snippet: An automation record is a finite family $R$ of generated material. Its entries may be event flows, theorem candidates, theorem genomes, candidate certificates, ledger entries, score certificates, or lineage edges. The record is an audit surface; it is not itself a classifier state.

label: def:automated-discovery-pipeline-state
title: Pipeline state
snippet: A pipeline state is a tuple $$ P=( T,R,,, w,B) $$ where $ T$ is a certified theory state, $R$ is an automation record, $$ is a population of theorem genomes, $$ is a lineage ledger, $ w N^9$ is a public theorem-genome weight profile, and $B: N$ is a genome-budget function.

label: def:automated-discovery-genome-extractor
title: Genome extractor
snippet: A genome extractor is a partial operation $$ Extract: $$ whose value, when defined on a theorem candidate flow $T$, is a theorem genome $(T,R,D_R(T))$ with all eight theorem-DNA loci. A theorem candidate is DNA-complete when $Extract(T)$ is defined.

label: def:automated-discovery-score-certificate
title: Score certificate
snippet: For a genome $$ in a pipeline state, a score certificate consists of the public weight profile $ w$, the budget value $B()$, and the inequality $$ Score_{ w}() B(). $$ It certifies a visible upper bound, not minimality.

label: def:automated-discovery-pipeline-transition
title: Pipeline transition
snippet: A pipeline transition is a change $$ P P' $$ between states $$ P=( T,R,,, w,B), P'=( T',R',',', w',B'). $$ Unless the transition explicitly changes the scoring protocol, the weight profile is held fixed.

label: def:automated-discovery-mechanical-expansion
title: Mechanical expansion
snippet: A transition is a mechanical expansion when $ T'= T$ and $R'$ is obtained from $R$ by adding material generated under the same classifier state. It may extend the record, but it does not change the certified classifier.

label: def:automated-discovery-genome-compression
title: Genome compression
snippet: A transition is a genome compression when $ T'= T$ and some genome mutation satisfies $$ Score_{ w}(')< Score_{ w}() $$ while the theorem classifier phenotype is unchanged.

label: def:automated-discovery-genome-recombination
title: Genome recombination
snippet: A genome recombination combines loci from parent genomes $_1,,_k$ and yields a child genome $'$ only when the child again satisfies theorem-genome soundness. Locus exchange without a soundness witness is only a candidate recombination.

label: def:automated-discovery-classifier-shift
title: Classifier-shift transition
snippet: A transition is a classifier-shift transition when $$ ( T_{cls} T') $$ holds on the common source carrier. It changes the classifier coordinate, regardless of whether the record length or genome score decreases.

label: def:automated-discovery-discovery-transition
title: Discovery transition
snippet: A classifier-shift transition is a discovery transition when the target theory state is certified and ledgered: $$ T'=(S',P',L',C',N'), N':(S',P',L',C'), $$ and $$ h:,\;L'(h). $$

label: def:automated-discovery-positive-discovery-transition
title: Positive discovery transition
snippet: Relative to an external cost observer $$ and transition cost $$, a discovery transition is positive when some finite family $X$ satisfies $$ _{ T'}(X)+( T T') < _{ T}(X). $$ The inequality charges the certificate, ledger, recognizer, and seal costs to the transition rather than hiding them in prose.

label: def:automated-discovery-claim
title: Discovery claim
snippet: A discovery claim is an audit packet $$ Claim= (K,, T, T',d,N',L', w,B,, B) $$ where $K$ is a claim kind, $$ is the principal genome, $ T, T'$ are source and target theory states, $d\{0,1\}$ is the classifier-change bit, $N'$ and $L'$ are the target certificate and ledger policy, $ w$ and $B$ are the scoring protocol, $$ is the lineage ledger, and $ B$ is the explicit not-claimed boundary.

label: def:automated-discovery-claim-kinds
title: Claim kinds
snippet: The claim kinds are $$ mechanical, compression, recombination, classifierShift, discovery, positiveDiscovery. $$ They respectively name record extension, score reduction without phenotype change, locus recombination, classifier change, ledgered certified classifier change, and ledgered certified classifier change with net compression gain.

label: def:automated-discovery-well-formed-claim
title: Well-formed claim
snippet: A claim is well formed when its kind matches its evidence: mechanical claims do not assert classifier change; compression claims carry a score comparison under a public weight profile and have $d=0$; classifier-shift claims have $d=1$; discovery claims have $d=1$, a target semantic naming certificate, and a ledger witness; positive-discovery claims additionally carry the net compression inequality. Any theorem-like principal object must be DNA-complete, and any scored claim must expose its weigh

label: def:automated-discovery-gate
title: Discovery gate
snippet: The predicate $DiscoveryGate(Claim)$ holds when the claim is well formed, its principal theorem-like object is a DNA-complete genome, it has a score certificate whenever it is scored, its discovery assertions carry semantic naming certificate and ledger witnesses, its positive-discovery assertions carry the net cost inequality, its lineage ledger records the parents and transition kind, its not-claimed boundary is explicit, and its support is formal or certificate-level rather than prose-only.

label: def:automated-discovery-gate-demotion
title: Gate demotion
snippet: Gate demotion maps an over-strong claim kind to the strongest kind supported by the available evidence. A positive-discovery claim without the cost inequality is treated as discovery at most; a discovery claim without certificate or ledger is treated as classifier-shift at most; a classifier-shift claim with $d=0$ is treated as compression or mechanical; an unscored compression claim is treated as an unscored mutation; a DNA-incomplete theorem-like object is treated as a theorem candidate.

label: thm:automated-discovery-dna-completeness-obligation
title: DNA completeness is a gate obligation
snippet: A theorem candidate that is not DNA-complete cannot be the principal theorem genome of a gate-passed discovery claim.

label: cor:automated-discovery-statement-code-insufficient
title: Statement-only and code-only candidates are insufficient
snippet: A candidate supplying only a statement locus, or only legal theorem code, does not pass the discovery gate as a theorem genome.

label: thm:automated-discovery-mechanical-not-discovery
title: Mechanical expansion is not discovery
snippet: Mechanical expansion does not imply discovery.

label: thm:automated-discovery-compression-not-discovery
title: Genome compression is not discovery by itself
snippet: Genome compression without classifier change is not discovery.

label: thm:automated-discovery-certificate-ledger-required

snippet: If a transition is a discovery transition with target state $ T'=(S',P',L',C',N')$, then $$ N':(S',P',L',C') $$ and $$ h:,\;L'(h). $$

label: thm:automated-discovery-positive-implies-discovery
title: Positive discovery implies discovery
snippet: Every positive discovery transition is a discovery transition.

label: thm:automated-discovery-scored-claims-public-weights
title: Scored claims require public weights
snippet: Any claim asserting a genome score, a score reduction, or a positive-discovery cost inequality must expose the weight profile used for the comparison.

label: thm:automated-discovery-gate-kind-sound
title: Discovery gate is kind-sound
snippet: If $DiscoveryGate(Claim)$ holds, then the obligations attached to the claim kind hold.

label: thm:automated-discovery-demotion-soundness
title: Demotion preserves audit soundness
snippet: After gate demotion, the resulting claim kind is no stronger than the evidence actually supplied by the claim.

label: def:automated-discovery-lineage-ledger
title: Lineage ledger
snippet: A lineage ledger is a directed acyclic graph $=(V,E)$ whose vertices are theorem genomes and whose edges are labelled by transition kind: mechanical, compression, recombination, classifier-shift, discovery, or positive-discovery.

label: def:automated-discovery-lineage-consistent-claim
title: Lineage-consistent claim
snippet: A claim is lineage-consistent when its parent genomes, child genome, and transition kind are recorded in $$ and the resulting ledger remains acyclic.

label: thm:automated-discovery-lineage-dag

snippet: If every accepted claim is lineage-consistent, the accepted theorem genomes form an auditable directed acyclic lineage graph.

label: def:automated-discovery-potential
title: Discovery potential
snippet: For selection among candidate genomes, a discovery-potential functional has the form $$ DP()= \,Cls() +\,Unification() +\,Reuse() +\,Transfer() -\,Score_{ w}() -\,LedgerRisk(). $$ Here $Cls$ records classifier change, while the remaining positive terms record unification, reuse, and transfer. The negative terms charge complexity and ledger risk.

label: thm:automated-discovery-lowest-score-not-best-target
title: Lowest score need not be the best discovery target
snippet: A genome with lower score can have lower discovery potential than a genome with higher score.

label: thm:automated-discovery-selection-favours-classifier-change
title: Classifier change is favoured when other terms are fixed
snippet: If a selection operator maximizes $DP$ and $>0$, then among candidates equal in all other coordinates it favours the candidate with classifier change.

label: def:automated-discovery-unpaid-discovery-claim
title: Unpaid discovery claim
snippet: An unpaid discovery claim is a claim that asserts discovery while lacking at least one of classifier change, semantic naming certificate, ledger witness, theorem genome, score or cost account, lineage witness, or not-claimed boundary.

label: thm:automated-discovery-no-unpaid-discovery
title: No unpaid discovery passes the gate
snippet: No unpaid discovery claim passes $DiscoveryGate$.

label: thm:automated-discovery-pipeline-safety
title: Pipeline safety
snippet: If an automated pipeline accepts discovery and positive-discovery claims only after $DiscoveryGate$ and records accepted claims in a lineage-consistent ledger, then every accepted discovery has classifier change, semantic naming certificate, ledger witness, DNA-complete theorem genome, score certificate, lineage witness, and an explicit not-claimed boundary.

label: thm:automated-discovery-pipeline-theorem
title: Automated theory-discovery pipeline theorem
snippet: An automated theory-discovery pipeline that extracts theorem genomes, exposes public scoring weights, demotes unsupported claim kinds, gates discovery claims, and records accepted claims in a lineage ledger distinguishes record growth, score reduction, recombination, classifier change, and ledgered discovery.
